brief: Goldman Sachs's weekly cross-asset note says markets are repricing around higher rates and oil prices. Last week the Fed and the BoJ each hiked policy rates by 25bps (Japan's rate is now the highest in over 31 years), while the BoE held rates steady. Front-end rates led the repricing, pushing G4 front-end volatility above equity volatility, while long-end yields stayed anchored by Treasury buybacks, hawkish BoJ pricing and UK gilt-friendly QT, leaving the US 2s10s curve at its flattest since March 2025. Brent crude moved back above $100/bbl on supply disruptions, warfare and refining constraints before moderating the same day. Goldman's Risk Appetite Indicator softened from its August peak, rebounding to 0.8, with the safe-versus-risky-asset gap at its widest since 2022; long bonds, the dollar and US IG CDS rebounded while non-US equities and the yen lagged, and global equities modestly de-rated despite higher commodity prices. The firm stays neutral across assets for 3 months and modestly pro-risk for 12 months (OW equities, UW credit), and in a rates-relief scenario expects credit, bond, real estate and equity hedges, plus receiver swaptions, to benefit from lower rates and oil prices.
